title: Accessing values through Weak pointers
prompt: Why can you not dereference a `Weak` pointer directly, and what method must you call instead?
answer: A `Weak` pointer does not prevent its referenced data from being dropped by `Rc`. Calling `.upgrade()` on a `Weak` pointer returns an `Option<Rc<T>>`. If the value was already dropped, `.upgrade()` returns `None`.
